identity.name: POWER GRID CORP. LTD.
identity.industry: Regulated Power-Transmission Utility (inter-state grid monopoly + TBCB)

summary.oneLiner: India's leading company in bulk power transmission, operating one of the world's largest EHVAC/HVDC transmission networks owned by a single entity, alongside consultancy, telecom (PowerTel) and emerging energy businesses.
summary.business: POWERGRID develops, owns and operates India's inter-state and intra-state bulk power transmission network using 765kV/400kV EHVAC substations and LCC/VSC based HVDC links, and is the executing agency for cross-border interconnections with neighbouring countries. It also provides specialised power-sector consultancy to domestic and international clients, offers telecom services through wholly owned subsidiary PowerTel on its pan-India optical ground wire network, and through subsidiary PESL has taken up pilot projects in solar generation, smart metering, BESS and green hydrogen.

currentContext.strengths: India's leading bulk power transmission company, operating one of the world's largest power transmission networks owned by a single entity|Deep power-sector tech-managerial expertise monetised as consultancy to over 150 domestic and 25 international clients across 25 countries|PowerTel is the only telecom service provider with a pan-India overhead optic fibre network on Extra High Voltage Transmission Lines|Ranked in the First Quadrant among leading global transmission utilities in a global benchmarking study on Asset Management and Operations & Maintenance|Consistently rated 'Excellent' under the MoU with the Government of India every year since FY1993-94|High system reliability track record: transmission system availability of 99.84% with trippings per line restricted to 0.26 in FY26
currentContext.strategies: Advancing a structural simplification initiative to build a leaner, more efficient organization by merging/consolidating TBCB SPVs.|Deepening digitalization of project execution and asset management through in-house platforms (e.g. PG Nirman), real-time project monitoring centres, AI-based tower defect detection and drone-based patrolling.|Building AI/ML capability in-house, including a customised Post Graduate Diploma programme with a reputed academic institution, to accelerate innovation across operations, assets and projects.|Diversifying beyond core transmission into new energy verticals -- Battery Energy Storage Systems, green hydrogen, solar power generation and smart metering -- through subsidiary PESL.|Expanding the telecom and digital business (PowerTel) into Data Centre services, building on its pan-India OPGW backbone.|Pursuing international expansion as a project developer (not just consultancy), evidenced by the Kenya Transmission PPP Project SPV and Africa50 agreement, and continued cross-border interconnection development.|Sustaining leadership in competitively bid (TBCB) transmission projects while retaining a large Regulated Tariff Mechanism (RTM) asset base for regulatory stability.|Maintaining highest priority on safety while sustaining a strong pace of project execution.|Pursuing ESG Vision 2030 -- transition to low-carbon operations, conscious consumption of natural resources, and a nurturing workplace -- anchored in the Environment and Social Policy & Procedures framework in place since 1998 and the ESG Policy adopted in 2023.
currentContext.expansion: During FY26 the Company added nine substations, taking its total to 291, with key additions at Bhadla, Ramgarh and Dausa (Rajasthan) to evacuate power from renewable-energy-rich areas, and commissioning of the KPS-2 and KPS-3 substations tied to the Khavda Renewable Energy Evacuation System in Gujarat. Several green-energy evacuation corridors were also commissioned, including Bhadla-Sikar, Ahmedabad-Lakadia and Ahmedabad-Navsari. India's first indigenously manufactured 400kV insulated cross-arm was developed and deployed to ease Right-of-Way constraints on new lines. POWERGRID Bellary Davanagere Transmission Limited (PBDTL), acquired via TBCB on 12 February 2026, is implementing transmission-system strengthening to integrate additional renewable capacity at Davanagere (0.25 GW) and Bellary (2.75 GW), with a CERC transmission licence application pending. Through wholly owned subsidiary PowerTel, the Company is expanding into Data Centre services: a commercial Data Centre at the POWERGRID Manesar Substation (Haryana) is under implementation, and land has been acquired in Chennai for a Zone-2 Data Centre. During the year the Company secured nine TBCB transmission projects and its first-ever Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project in Andhra Pradesh. For FY27, several renewable-energy evacuation projects are slated for completion, including substations at Kopal, Gadag, Vataman, Kurnool-III and Ananthpuram with their associated transmission networks, against a stated FY27 capex target of approximately Rs 37,000 crore and a capitalisation target of approximately Rs 30,000 crore. On the technology/R&D side, the Company commissioned a 400kV, 315 MVA synthetic ester oil-filled transformer (Asia's first) for improved environmental safety, launched a programme to develop domestic suppliers for high-voltage Emergency Restoration System (ERS) components up to 400kV that were previously imported, and established a POWERGRID Centre of Excellence in Cyber Security at a premier institute for R&D on Operational Technology security in transmission and grid operations.
currentContext.mdna: India's per-capita electricity consumption is expected to rise from about 1,541 kWh in 2024 to around 2,000 kWh by 2030, over 4,000 kWh by 2047, and 7,000-10,000 kWh by 2070, necessitating sustained power infrastructure development.|Energy demand is expected to grow at the fastest rate among major economies, driven by urbanisation, industrialisation, electric mobility, energy-intensive technologies, digital infrastructure and green hydrogen production.|Per the Mid-Term Review of the 20th Electric Power Survey, peak electricity demand is projected to rise from 289 GW (2026-27) to 345 GW (2029-30) and further to 388 GW (2031-32); the country has already seen new all-time peak demand records since April 2026, reaching 270.8 GW on May 21, 2026.|Data Centres and Green Hydrogen are emerging as new large demand centres -- AI-led data-centre clusters are coming up as large concentrated point loads, while green hydrogen is expected to add approximately 71 GW of demand by 2032; India's data-centre capacity of around 1,280 MW is projected to expand four to five times by 2030.|India's power sector is on a multi-decade investment cycle in which transmission has evolved into a platform empowering the energy transition, underpinned by the Central Electricity Authority's plan to integrate over 900 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2035-36.|Development of about 76 GW of hydropower capacity across 12 sub-basins of the Brahmaputra is viewed as another major driver of transmission expansion.|Grid-scale battery energy storage is becoming central to grid utilisation, with cumulative BESS capacity rising sharply and industry estimates placing India's cumulative storage requirement at about 888 GWh by 2035-36, requiring close integration with the transmission network.|Cross-border power transfer capacity with neighbouring countries is expected to rise from about 10 GW currently to about 26 GW going forward, supporting regional power exchange.|A large and growing portfolio of Regulated Tariff Mechanism (RTM) assets continues to provide regulatory stability alongside the Company's competitively bid (TBCB) project leadership.|Works in hand of approximately ₹1.7 lakh crore, including CWIP of ₹0.48 lakh crore, together with a bidding pipeline in excess of ₹1.1 lakh crore, provide strong multi-year execution visibility.|The wider Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) sector opportunity per CTUIL's Rolling Plan 2030-31 comprises 77,228 ckm of transmission lines and 6,97,747 MVA of transformation capacity at an estimated cost of ₹5,41,481 crore over the next five years, of which ~42,000 ckm/414 GVA (~₹2.83 lakh crore) is under construction and ~34,400 ckm/284 GVA (~₹2.58 lakh crore) is under planning/approval/bidding.

risks.note: The bulk of revenue is earned under the Regulated Tariff Mechanism, where transmission charges (Return on Equity, depreciation, O&M recovery, interest on working capital) are set by CERC-notified regulations that reset periodically; the new CERC (Terms and Conditions of Tariff) Regulations, 2024 for the 2024-29 tariff block reduced the base Return on Equity for assets commissioned on or after 1 April 2024 to 15.0% (pre-tax gross-up) versus 15.5% protected for pre-2024 assets, showing that future tariff-block resets can directly move realised returns.

Transmission and transmission-related activities constituted 85.14% of total income in FY26, leaving the Company's results highly dependent on the regulatory and demand dynamics of a single core business line despite diversification efforts in telecom, consultancy and new energy verticals.

risks.risk: Regulatory/licensing non-approval risk on specific assets
risks.note: CERC has, in the past, withdrawn regulatory approval for a transmission project element: for POWERGRID Vemagiri Transmission Limited, CERC's order dated 6 April 2015 held that the Vemagiri-Khammam-Hyderabad 765kV D/C lines were neither required as an evacuation line nor a system-strengthening line and withdrew the licence/regulatory approval for that transmission project, illustrating exposure to regulator determinations that can strand or invalidate specific project revenue.

Management's own Enterprise Risk Management framework spans strategic, operational, financial, HR, compliance, sustainability and information/cyber-security risk domains across the organisation, reviewed by a Board-level Risk Management Committee (convened three times in FY26) and a Chief Risk Officer, indicating risk is broad-based rather than confined to a single identifiable driver.

one-line thesis: A regulated-return monopoly grid utility inflecting into a multi-year capex super-cycle (capex up ~4x to ~Rs35,000 cr in 3 yrs, guiding Rs37–45k cr FY27), riding India's RE-evacuation + AI/data-center demand build-out, with execution bottlenecks (RoW, transformers, manpower) reportedly easing.

One-offs: none material flagged; force-majeure/land-diminution cost escalations being recovered via additional CERC tariff (pass-through).
guidance (next periods):
- **Capex:** FY27 Rs37,000 cr (committed to GoI; "definitely more"), guided up to Rs45,000 cr; long-run FY29-36 average ~Rs40,000 cr/yr.
- **Capitalization:** FY27 Rs30,000 cr; FY28 Rs35,000 cr; ~Rs65,000 cr cumulative over next 2 yrs.
- Mgmt explicitly DID NOT raise FY27/FY28 capex guidance despite beating FY26 — said guidance is based only on projects-in-hand and would be revised mid-FY27 as new wins land. (Some analysts disappointed by no upward revision.)
- Equity-funding: ~Rs12-14k cr equity need at 20% on Rs60-70k cr capex; comfortably covered by rising PAT (Rs17-20k cr) net of ~Rs5,000 cr dividend; willing to flex equity to 18-19% if needed.
order book & pipeline:
- **Works in hand: ~Rs1,48,000 cr** (incl. ~Rs49,000 cr CWIP) → net ~Rs1,00,000 cr practical capex; **excludes** the fluid Leh/Pang-Kaithal (~Rs23,000-25,000 cr) HVDC project (may convert to AC; removed from guidance until re-awarded).
- TBCB win rate >50% historically; targeting to maintain ~50%.
- Long-run opportunity: ~Rs7.9 lakh cr CEA FY27-36 transmission plan; +Rs3-4 lakh cr cross-border (OSOWOG); +Rs4 lakh cr Brahmaputra basin HVDC → total ~Rs15 lakh cr visibility. At 50% share → ~Rs6-9 lakh cr to 2035 (~Rs60,000 cr/yr).
- Rajasthan RE evacuation: 73 GW of 115 GW planned tendered; beyond-73 GW (incl. Bhadla-Fatehpur, Barmer-South Olpad HVDC) was stuck on HVDC landing-point/demand finalization; CTUIL now releasing AC + HVDC + 1100/1200 kV projects (MP, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Odisha, AP).
segment / subsidiary (spv restructuring):
- 19 SPVs → 2 SPVs merger: MCA approval received.
- Next: 28 wholly-owned subsidiaries → 2 WOS (board approved; going to MoP).
- DIPAM per-SPV equity cap raised Rs5,000 → Rs7,500 cr; PG lobbying for Rs10,000-15,000 cr to merge more. ~78 entities today, could double given pipeline.
- CFO: merger is for governance/administrative control, NOT cost savings; lines function independently, licenses unchanged; no quantified savings.
growth verticals / optionality:
- HVDC & 1200 kV backbone leadership (11 HVDC projects; world's largest 765 kv network; 1200 kv developed in-house 2012).
- Cross-border interconnects (OSOWOG: UAE, Saudi, Oman, Sri Lanka, Singapore, Maldives, Myanmar) — 2-3 yrs out, gov-level talks.
- Brahmaputra basin (~35,000+ MW Arunachal hydro; Niglok / lower Subansiri / Biswanath Chariali; 800 kv HVDC) — bidding in ~1 yr.
- BESS: participating but winning poorly vs smaller players (only 1 project); reworking methodology + advance tie-ups with battery suppliers.
- Intra-state: participating but de-prioritized (small projects, similar effort to large).
margins & cost dynamics:
- Regulated RoE model insulates returns; TBCB cost escalation (land-diminution, force-majeure) recoverable via additional CERC tariff → no IRR hit expected.
- Reliability/digital: AI-based defect detection, drone patrolling, predictive maintenance → 99.84% availability.
capex / expansion:
- Capex ramp: ~Rs8-9k cr (FY22-23) → Rs12,500 cr (FY24) → Rs26,000 cr (FY25) → Rs35,000+ cr (FY26); >Rs1,00,000 cr cumulative last 5 yrs; >Rs90,000 cr capitalized FY21-26.
- Execution-capacity expansion: 5 (→7) skill centers training ~350 fitters/qtr → ~1,400-1,500/yr → ~100+ erection gangs/yr.
capital allocation:
- >Rs50,000 cr dividends paid FY21-26; dividend yield ~3-4%; ~Rs5,000 cr compulsory annual payout in funding math.
- 45% institutional ownership.
- Self-funds growth via rising PAT + debt at ~80:20 D:E; no equity dilution signalled.
risks & watch-items:
- Guidance conservatism / no upward FY27-28 revision despite FY26 beat → near-term tendering visibility soft.
- Tendering slowdown beyond 73 GW Rajasthan (now reportedly resolving) — pipeline lumpiness risk.
- RoW remains a "perpetual challenge" despite improved GoI compensation guidelines (rural 30% / semi-urban 45% / urban 60% premium).
- Transformer/reactor supply, skilled manpower — addressed but historically caused delays (recent AC projects took 3-3.5 yrs vs 18-mo bids).
- New project timelines normalized to 30-36 months (vs unrealistic 18-24) → slower per-project capitalization cadence.
- BESS competitive weakness vs smaller players.
- Leadership transition: CMD Tyagi retiring (superannuation).
- Summer FY27 demand ~270-275 GW; possible El Niño / gas / hydro deficit (macro, not company-specific).
management quality / tone: Confident, visionary, "nation-building to 2047" framing; strong on operational metrics and execution-capability narrative. Heavy on opportunity-size (Rs15 lakh cr TAM) but candid on guidance being projects-in-hand only. CFO measured/honest (no cost savings claimed on merger). Retiring CMD's valedictory tone.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The FY26 capex/capitalization beat is largely commissioning-timing driven (Navsari-Phadge, Bikaner-III sliding into late March) — lumpy, not run-rate.
- Pang-Kaithal (Leh) ~Rs23-25k cr REMOVED from order book — material de-risking/haircut to the headline pipeline; watch for re-award (AC vs HVDC undecided).
- New Rs7.9 lakh cr CEA plan (FY27-36, released 19-Mar at Bharat Electricity Summit) is incremental to existing ongoing projects, not a replacement — but specifics/awarding timeline unknown ("after some time").
- SPV mergers deliver governance optics, not P&L — don't model cost savings.
- 30-36 month project timelines = structurally slower capitalization conversion than bull-case assumes.
- GIB (Great Indian Bustard) Supreme Court ruling: NO impact on PG's Rajasthan/Ramgarh/Bhadla projects (all outside GIB zone) — removes an overhang.

- Cross-border interconnects (OSOWOG: UAE, Saudi, Oman, Sri Lanka, Singapore, Maldives, Myanmar) — 2-3 yrs out, gov-level talks.
- Brahmaputra basin (~35,000+ MW Arunachal hydro; Niglok / lower Subansiri / Biswanath Chariali; 800 kv HVDC) — bidding in ~1 yr.
- BESS: participating but winning poorly vs smaller players (only 1 project); reworking methodology + advance tie-ups with battery suppliers.
- Intra-state: participating but de-prioritized (small projects, similar effort to large).
margins & cost dynamics:
- Regulated RoE model insulates returns; TBCB cost escalation (land-diminution, force-majeure) recoverable via additional CERC tariff → no IRR hit expected.
- Reliability/digital: AI-based defect detection, drone patrolling, predictive maintenance → 99.84% availability.
capex / expansion:
- Capex ramp: ~Rs8-9k cr (FY22-23) → Rs12,500 cr (FY24) → Rs26,000 cr (FY25) → Rs35,000+ cr (FY26); >Rs1,00,000 cr cumulative last 5 yrs; >Rs90,000 cr capitalized FY21-26.
- Execution-capacity expansion: 5 (→7) skill centers training ~350 fitters/qtr → ~1,400-1,500/yr → ~100+ erection gangs/yr.
capital allocation:
- >Rs50,000 cr dividends paid FY21-26; dividend yield ~3-4%; ~Rs5,000 cr compulsory annual payout in funding math.
- 45% institutional ownership.
- Self-funds growth via rising PAT + debt at ~80:20 D:E; no equity dilution signalled.
risks & watch-items:
- Guidance conservatism / no upward FY27-28 revision despite FY26 beat → near-term tendering visibility soft.
- Tendering slowdown beyond 73 GW Rajasthan (now reportedly resolving) — pipeline lumpiness risk.
- RoW remains a "perpetual challenge" despite improved GoI compensation guidelines (rural 30% / semi-urban 45% / urban 60% premium).
- Transformer/reactor supply, skilled manpower — addressed but historically caused delays (recent AC projects took 3-3.5 yrs vs 18-mo bids).
- New project timelines normalized to 30-36 months (vs unrealistic 18-24) → slower per-project capitalization cadence.
- BESS competitive weakness vs smaller players.
- Leadership transition: CMD Tyagi retiring (superannuation).
- Summer FY27 demand ~270-275 GW; possible El Niño / gas / hydro deficit (macro, not company-specific).
management quality / tone: Confident, visionary, "nation-building to 2047" framing; strong on operational metrics and execution-capability narrative. Heavy on opportunity-size (Rs15 lakh cr TAM) but candid on guidance being projects-in-hand only. CFO measured/honest (no cost savings claimed on merger). Retiring CMD's valedictory tone.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The FY26 capex/capitalization beat is largely commissioning-timing driven (Navsari-Phadge, Bikaner-III sliding into late March) — lumpy, not run-rate.
- Pang-Kaithal (Leh) ~Rs23-25k cr REMOVED from order book — material de-risking/haircut to the headline pipeline; watch for re-award (AC vs HVDC undecided).
- New Rs7.9 lakh cr CEA plan (FY27-36, released 19-Mar at Bharat Electricity Summit) is incremental to existing ongoing projects, not a replacement — but specifics/awarding timeline unknown ("after some time").
- SPV mergers deliver governance optics, not P&L — don't model cost savings.
- 30-36 month project timelines = structurally slower capitalization conversion than bull-case assumes.
- GIB (Great Indian Bustard) Supreme Court ruling: NO impact on PG's Rajasthan/Ramgarh/Bhadla projects (all outside GIB zone) — removes an overhang.

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.
